# GrowthBook Entitlements Pricing and Security Review
Date: 2026-11-20 | Duration: 27.020000457763672m

## Summary
Fuel Finance uses self-hosted GrowthBook for development flags and client entitlements rather than A/B testing, with current functionality covering roughly 75% of its needs. Feature flags and targeting rules support client-specific access, trials, and tier previews, but sales-friendly Bronze or Gold controls would require an admin panel, CRM integration, or API-based group updates. Fuel Finance has already built an internal wrapper and entitlement system, reducing the value of enterprise functionality. The main unresolved issue is security: one shared API key can affect flags across environments, so environment-specific permissions are unavailable. A proxy or additional server layer could shield production credentials, with Oleg estimating roughly $3k for implementation and an annual ceiling of approximately $12k. GrowthBook enterprise self-hosting was discussed at $175k annually, with a proposed discount reducing the next-year cost to $50k, but this remained outside Fuel Finance’s budget. Christian planned to reassess pricing, while Oleg planned to validate the internal security approach.

## Keywords
Feature entitlements, API-key security, Self-hosted Enterprise, Environment isolation, Controlled customer pilots, Pricing negotiation
